hits.author: marit
hits.comment_text:
It does: a rename writes the new entry first and clears the old one last, so a cut leaves you with two names for one file, never none. The check at mount time removes the older one:

for entry in directory:
    if entry.block in seen:
        drop(older(entry, seen[entry.block]))
    seen[entry.block] = entry

hits.author: duty_cycle
hits.comment_text:
We ship something close to this on a sensor that wakes twice a day. Two years in the field, about 4000 units, no corrupt cards so far. The part people underestimate is wear: with so few blocks you rewrite the same ones very often.

Our fix was dull and it works: rotate the directory through eight blocks and keep a counter to find the newest.

Details: https://iot.example.com/wear-notes
